title: Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes and the No-FOMO Action Plan
web_title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes and the No-FOMO Action Plan
question: Which facts could make this operating platform worth more, and which could break the per-share cash case?

epigraph.quote: Our financial results and improved outlook enable us to further raise our guidance ranges for 2026.
epigraph.author: Jack Fusco, CEO, Q3 2026 results release [3]

web_blocks.text: The bull case starts with physical execution. Cheniere completed the seventh CCL Stage 3 train in August 2026 ahead of its guaranteed schedule and within budget, raised its 2026 financial ranges after Q3, and signed new long-term SPAs with Petrobras and QatarEnergy. Those facts extend the operating and commercial platform; they do not prove that future expansion capital will earn attractive returns. [3][10][13]

The strongest bear case is not that LNG demand vanishes. It is that a capital-intensive, levered exporter can move contracted tonnes and still deliver uneven per-share cash when derivative marks, cargo timing, project debt, outside ownership and expansion capex work against common shareholders. Nine-month 2026 GAAP income fell despite higher export volume and adjusted EBITDA, making cash conversion and project returns the key downside tests. [2][3][20]

web_blocks.caption: Steelman: strongest evidence on each side and the falsifier to monitor
rows: New 2026 agreements add nearly 5 mtpa of long-term sales; year-end 2025 average remaining contract life was about 15 years. [2][3]
New global supply increases buyer choice; future SPAs may require lower fees, more flexibility or greater seller exposure. [2][18][30]
CCL Stage 3 completed ahead of schedule and within budget; Q3 volumes rose year over year. [3][10]
Commissioning is not a full year of stable utilization. Outages, maintenance, feed gas, pipeline limits and weather can reduce cargoes. [2][3]
9M 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was $6.037B and DCF $4.07B; management raised full-year ranges. [3]
9M attributable GAAP net income was $736M versus $3.028B a year earlier, principally after $3.6B of unfavorable derivative variance. DCF is non-GAAP and does not deduct all growth capex. [3][20]
Available liquidity was $8.079B including cash and undrawn facilities; brownfield projects can be phased. [3]
Debt, lease liabilities, noncontrolling interests and expansion obligations reduce cash available to common owners. Liquidity is not the same as parent cash. [2][3][20]
web_blocks.takeaway: The bull case is execution plus contracted visibility. The bear case is weaker per-share cash conversion if derivative timing, expansion spending or new supply erodes the cash yield.

web_blocks.text: The scenario weights are analyst assumptions applied to Q3 midpoint DCF guidance and the Q3 diluted weighted-average share proxy. Bear: DCF 20% below midpoint at 8x P/DCF; base: midpoint at 11x; bull: DCF growth of 15% at 12x. Neither probabilities nor valuation multiples come from management or consensus. [3][20]

web_blocks.takeaway: The expected price outcome is only 3.8% above the 12 Nov close before dividends and taxes; base-case reward-to-risk is 0.82:1 at the close and 2.04:1 at the upper edge of the proposed support band.

web_blocks.text: The new-capital verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. The stock remains Stage 2, but the market is in Correction and LNG gained 10.70% in the prior week. The medium-term inflection is the CCL Stage 3 ramp and management’s preliminary 2027 production outlook of 56–58 million tonnes, including roughly 52 million tonnes expected under long-term contracts. The long-term compounding case remains conditional on reliable operations, contract economics and disciplined project returns. [8][10][12][24]

The current holding decision is separate. The same-session positions ledger shows 6.2472 Schwab shares, $1,933.38 market value, $1,999.95 cost basis and a $66.57 unrealized loss. The position is 2.13% of $90,686.77 net worth. Its size is modest and Stage 2 has not broken, so retain the shares with a hard-stop alert rather than selling solely to realize a small loss. [12]

The redeployment decision concerns the next marginal cash unit; no sale proceeds are being created. Keep 100% in cash at the current price. LNG remains the only directly underwritten shortlist candidate in this single-company run; it receives 0% until support and operating conditions align. Chapter 7 comparators are not fully re-underwritten alternatives, so no outside name receives capital by implication.

Revisit new capital after a completed close returns to $284.10–$297.07, the $6.05B DCF floor remains credible, Stage 2 support holds and the market regime does not worsen. Re-underwrite immediately if FY2026 DCF falls below $6.05B, Stage 3 ramp misses, project financing or permits materially change, or a completed daily close falls below $278.52. [3][12][20]

web_blocks.intro: No new share allocation is recommended at the 12 November close. The deterministic risk-unit table is a reference for a future support-zone review, not an order ticket.

book_paragraphs: The bull case deserves more than a slogan. Cheniere operates two large Gulf Coast sites, has a long cargo-delivery record, and completed the last CCL Stage 3 train ahead of its guaranteed schedule and within budget. Q3 volumes rose and management raised its 2026 financial ranges. New agreements with Petrobras and QatarEnergy extend the customer book. These are real operating achievements; none guarantees the return on the next train. [3][10][13]

The strongest evidence is physical. A train moved from project financing through construction, first LNG and substantial completion. To keep the bull case alive, that capacity must become stable shipments and cash rather than remain a milestone in a release. The preliminary 2027 production outlook of 56–58 million tonnes creates a measurable next test, with about 52 million tonnes expected under long-term contracts. [3][8]

Now steelman the bear. Demand can grow while an investment disappoints if new supply strengthens buyers, global spreads normalize, commissioning takes longer or construction consumes cash before it produces. Existing contracts reduce near-term volume risk, but they do not fix every future fee or protect every project return. Cheniere itself describes competition for new and renewed agreements, while U.S. export capacity continues to expand. [2][18]

Earnings quality is the second bear pillar. In the first nine months of 2026, parent-attributable net income was $736 million, well below the comparable period. Management cited $3.6 billion of unfavorable derivative fair-value variance while reporting $6.037 billion of Adjusted EBITDA and $4.07 billion of DCF. Both adjusted measures help explain the operation, but neither is GAAP nor a promise of unrestricted cash after growth capital and outside ownership. [3][20]

The balance sheet makes the distinction important. At September 30, 2026, current and noncurrent debt exceeded $23 billion, compared with $1.663 billion of cash, alongside sizable lease liabilities. The reported $8.079 billion of available liquidity included undrawn facilities, not just cash at the parent. The platform can service obligations when assets perform; it remains exposed to refinancing terms, drawdowns, maintenance and new construction. [3][20]

The scenario math keeps our disagreement explicit. Bear assumes DCF 20% below the 2026 midpoint and an 8x multiple; base holds the $6.30 billion midpoint at 11x; bull assumes 15% growth at 12x. We assign 25%, 50% and 25%, respectively, producing a weighted value of $321.24, or 3.8% above the close before dividends. Every weight and multiple is ours, and DCF is a company-defined measure. [3][20]

This does not support fresh capital at the close. The base value of $334.94 is above $309.48, but only 0.82 times the downside distance to the $278.52 stop. A retracement to the $284.10–$297.07 band changes the geometry: the same target gives 2.04 times the risk from the band high. The recommendation is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT, not an indirect invitation to buy at market. [12]

The current owner faces a different decision. The ledger confirms 6.2472 shares in Schwab worth $1,933.38, against $1,999.95 cost. The unrealized loss is $66.57, and the position is 2.13% of consolidated net worth. With Stage 2 intact and no thesis-breaking fundamental event, we retain the modest holding under a hard stop. A completed close below $278.52 would change that instruction for all 6.2472 shares. [12]

For new money, the reviewed capital is the next marginal dollar of cash, not hypothetical sale proceeds. Keep it in cash until the entry and operating gates clear. LNG is the underwritten shortlist name in this report; outside comparators in the peer table were not researched to the same depth. The report therefore assigns neither an unearned allocation nor a hidden alternative recommendation. [12]

Short term, the trend is constructive but the market is in Correction, so wait for support. Medium term, watch cargoes against the 2027 production outlook and reconcile delivered volume with cash conversion. Long term, the platform compounds only if each incremental project earns an adequate return after financing, growth capital and noncontrolling interests. The business quality remains conditional, not a bond-like toll road. [2][3][8]

The hinge claim is that contract-backed cash remains durable enough to service obligations and fund maintenance while new capacity is phased rather than rushed. The filings support a large platform and a long customer book; the unresolved tests are full-year DCF, Stage 3 utilization and the commercial and capital package for each future phase. A DCF result below $6.05 billion, a sustained close below $278.52 or a materially weaker FID package requires a fresh underwriting. [2][3][12][20]

book_subsections.title: What changes the action
paragraphs: A completed close into $284.10–$297.07, with Stage 2 intact and DCF still on track, allows a small staged-entry review because the support-zone asymmetry clears the rule. A completed close below $278.52 invalidates the technical plan and triggers the hard-stop instruction for the current holding. These are advisory levels; confirm the latest close, corporate actions and overnight gap risk before acting. [3][12]

Fundamental event gates remain separate from chart levels. FY2026 results must reconcile DCF and adjusted EBITDA with GAAP earnings, derivative settlement and operating cash. CCL Stage 3 must become reliable output. Future projects must pass their own permitting, commercial, financing and FID gates. If any condition changes, rebuild the valuation before relying on its range.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Cheniere is neither a simple commodity bet nor a bond-like toll road. Its contracts create real visibility, while derivatives, capital, ownership and construction gates keep the cash promise conditional. Keep the modest position while the structure holds; keep new money in cash until price earns the required asymmetry.
